audit.why: 52.51% over 598 games. The chart gives Camille levels 2-3 and both item stages with the rest Skill, and the prose is blunt that a three-AP-item Vladimir cannot be solo-killed. That is the right shape for a scaling drain mage against a level-2 bully.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 entry covers only Camille's ultimate and the pool. Hemoplague is never mentioned anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Vladimir's level-6 ability is Hemoplague — a 120s zone that heals him and amplifies the damage everything else in his kit deals to anyone standing in it. Writing level 6 as 'lock him in the arena and stop him roaming' with the only caveat being Sanguine Pool leaves out the reason a 1v1 inside his own Hemoplague is a worse fight than the same 1v1 outside it. It also completes the sustain picture: _missing-interactions.json flags Transfusion and Hemoplague together as the reason Grievous Wounds decides extended trades here, and anti-heal appears nowhere in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Hemoplague named with its 120s cooldown and the Grievous Wounds cue added.

audit.whatIsWrong: Camille's passive is written as 'Adaptive Defense' in spikes[3].text and late, and her R without its article. Sanguine Pool's 'long cooldown' is invoked five times and never once quantified, and Tides of Blood is named exactly once with no mechanics attached.
audit.why: The pool is the whole matchup, so its number is the whole matchup: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and drops to 16s at rank 5. Against Hookshot's 16s and The Hextech Ultimatum's 140s, a rank-1 pool is a genuinely long window and a rank-5 pool is not — which is the real reason 'close the lane early' is correct advice rather than a platitude. Transfusion is 9s at rank 1 falling to 4.6s, so his sustain accelerates sharply as he ranks it, and Tides of Blood is 13s down to 5s.
audit.corrected: Adaptive Defenses and The Hextech Ultimatum given their real names; Sanguine Pool's 28s stated where the 'long cooldown' claim is made; Transfusion's ranking curve written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track his pool cooldown', 'on the long pool cooldown', 'force every trade while it's down' — the punishable cooldown is correctly identified three times over and never given.
audit.why: 28s at rank 1 is the single most actionable number in this lane and it is exactly what turns 'bait the pool' from an instruction into a plan. It also explains the decay: by the time he has ranked it and bought cooldown reduction, the window you were told to use no longer exists.
audit.corrected: 28s written into spikes[2].text, wants.you[1] and mid.

audit.why: The best fact in this matchup is already present and correctly stated: Sanguine Pool makes him untargetable, so it dodges the R cast itself, and the correct sequencing is to bait the pool with a poke first and only then commit the ultimate. That is precisely the kind of concrete cooldown-keyed instruction the rest of this champion's data is missing.

edits.before: Win the lane early, because this is the matchup that flips hard against you. A full-AP Vlad with Rylai's, Liandry's, and a Zhonya's pools your R the instant you leap, drains the trade back through your Adaptive Defense shield, and kites your short AA range until you're useless in the 1v1 — Sanguine Pool means your single-target R and E-stun can always be dodged with good timing. Your bruiser tempo peaks at first item; once he has two AP items you can't solo-kill him, so snowball your early lead onto the map and let your team handle the unkillable late-game Vlad rather than dueling him.
edits.after: Win the lane early, because this is the matchup that flips hard against you. A full-AP Vlad with Rylai's, Liandry's and a Zhonya's pools your R the instant you leap, drains the trade back through your Adaptive Defenses shield, and kites you out of the 1v1 — and by rank 5 Sanguine Pool is 16s, not 28s, so the window you were using is simply gone. Hemoplague heals him and amplifies everything his kit lands, so Grievous Wounds is the item that keeps you relevant. notes: Hemoplague was missing from the matchup entirely, which left the level-6 stage reading as a straight Camille spike and left anti-heal unmentioned despite _missing-interactions.json flagging Transfusion and Hemoplague sustain for this exact pairing. The other substantive gap was numeric: Sanguine Pool's 'long cooldown' is the pivot of five separate instructions and was never quantified — 28s at rank 1 decaying to 16s at rank 5 is also the argument for closing the lane early, so stating it makes the existing advice self-justifying. The untargetable-dodges-the-R-cast interaction was already correct and well written; I left it and only added the cooldown.
